columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: 1M+ audiobooks and podcasts, plus Audible Originals; expanding localized services to 11+ new global markets.
US plans (2026): Standard/Plus USD 8.99/mo (Plus catalog streaming); Premium Plus USD 14.95/mo (1 credit/month + Plus catalog); frequent Prime member promos.
Reports ~10x membership growth over the past decade and projects another ~125% growth over the next three years.

strengths.title: Extensive audiobook catalog and exclusives
strengths.detail: Industry-leading selection of audiobooks, Originals, and exclusive content, huge amount of books in audio format.

strengths.title: Flexible subscription and ownership model
strengths.detail: Credits buy premium titles you own permanently, plus streaming access to a large Plus catalog.

strengths.title: High production quality
strengths.detail: Many titles feature professional narration, multi-cast performances, and sound design.

strengths.title: Cross-device support
strengths.detail: iOS, Android, web, Alexa, and more, with offline downloads and sync.

weaknesses.title: Subscription complexity
weaknesses.detail: Credits vs Plus catalog vs purchased titles confuse many new users.

weaknesses.title: Credit-based limitations
weaknesses.detail: Premium Plus typically offers 1 credit per month, heavy listeners often need extra credits or à la carte purchases.

weaknesses.title: Cost compared to some alternatives
weaknesses.detail: For casual listeners, can feel expensive vs multi-title subscriptions like Everand.

weaknesses.title: Uneven catalog quality
weaknesses.detail: Large catalog includes lower-quality or poorly narrated titles alongside standouts.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Audible is audiobook catalog, credits, and narration, how many people “read” long-form audio. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Audible is the leading producer and provider of audio storytelling, offering customers a destination for audiobooks, podcasts, and exclusive Audible Originals.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Audible side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Audible you can use Audio, Memberships, and Marketplaces as first-class product jobs. You want a dedicated listening app, playlists, and the catalog people already pay a subscription for.

Using Kahana with Audible

You can use both. Audible keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep listening on Audible, where the catalog and players are strongest. Put episode lists, companion notes, and Club discussion on Kahana so assigned audio is a library item, not only a For You row.
